dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux; uses CALL to external subprograms like ORCSGDAY, ORCSDAY, and COPY of .INC files typical of ORCA system
evidence: no EXEC CICS or EXEC SQL

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (claims) processing system - periodic/regular billing (Teiki Seikyuu) subsystem for hospital/clinic administration
purpose.summary: This program (ORCGO01) is part of the JMA ORCA medical receipt software system. It handles periodic billing (Teiki Seikyuu) screen processing, including initialization, screen transitions, date conversion, and job management for regular medical insurance claim submissions. It manages SPA (screen persistent area) data, calls date-conversion and job-management subprograms, and coordinates multi-screen navigation.

notable_features: 27 COPY statements referencing .INC files typical of ORCA system
18 CALL statements to ORCA subprograms (ORCSGDAY, ORCSDAY, etc.)
LINKAGE SECTION with MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA
Japanese text in comments (encoded as latin-1/EUC-JP)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS - uses proprietary MCP middleware
File SELECT for TEIKIERR error file
verdict.notes: Comments contain Japanese text encoded in EUC-JP but decoded as latin-1, resulting in mojibake. The program uses JMA ORCA's proprietary MCP (Medical Care Platform) middleware rather than CICS, but program_type 'online-cics' is the closest match for an interactive screen-driven subprogram. Source truncated at 16000 chars; full program is 1482 lines.
